title: HISPANIC REUNIFICATION CANON
subtitle: From the Universal Monarchy and Iberian Union to Hispanidad, Patria Grande, Lusophony, and Iberofonía

source.principal_dossier: Research dossier: The Panhispanic and Pan-Iberian Canon, 1808-2026

methodological_thesis: Composite unity → political disaggregation → memory of unity → rival projects of reunification

bueno_classes.name: Nationalist alternative
bueno_classes.definition: The sovereign nation is the primary political reality; wider Hispanic, Latin American, Iberian, or Lusophone unity is secondary or superstructural.

bueno_classes.name: Inter-nationalist alternative
bueno_classes.definition: A universal doctrine or institution not generated by the Iberian-American historical field supplies the principle of unity.

bueno_classes.name: American / Latin American / Indo-American whole
bueno_classes.definition: America is treated as an attributive historical whole and the point of departure for a new project.

bueno_classes.name: Pan-American alternative
bueno_classes.definition: The Hispanic and Portuguese American republics are parts of a greater hemispheric system.

bueno_classes.name: Occidentalist alternative
bueno_classes.definition: The societies of the Iberian worlds are parts of Western civilization.

bueno_classes.name: Hispanist alternative
bueno_classes.definition: Spain, Spanish America, and other historically connected societies are parts of a greater Hispanic Community.

bueno_classes.name: Lusophone alternative
bueno_classes.definition: Portuguese-speaking societies are parts of a historically constituted Lusophone community; this is an extension beyond Bueno's numbered alternatives.

bueno_classes.name: Iberian / Iberophone alternative
bueno_classes.definition: Hispanic and Lusophone communities are parts of a larger pluricontinental Iberian-derived whole; this is an extension beyond Bueno's numbered alternatives.

unity_types.I→S: attempt to transform identity or similarity into organized relations

operations.name: Restoration
operations.definition: Reconstructs a previous synalogical order, or its governing identity of project, as the model of renewed unity.
operations.visual: Backward memory arc followed by a forward projection.

operations.name: Recomposition
operations.definition: Organizes constituted political units into a new synalogical whole while preserving their recognizable identities.
operations.visual: Separate lines converge on a federal, confederal, congressional, or allied node.

operations.name: Transfiguration
operations.definition: Transfers the material identity of unity from dynasty and sovereignty toward language, religion, law, literature, culture, memory, or civilizational purpose.
operations.visual: Diagonal broken trajectory across political and cultural fields.

operations.name: Refoundation
operations.definition: Reorganizes inherited historical materials as a new attributive whole under a new American, Indo-American, popular, socialist, anti-imperialist, or postcolonial project.
operations.visual: Forward trajectory arising from B1 rather than returning to a metropolitan center.

operations.name: Rearticulation
operations.definition: Renews synalogical relations among independent parts without requiring one federation, state, or sovereign authority.
operations.visual: Linked constellation among institutions and independent political centers.
